questions.question: Which of the following instruments is used for measuring radiation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Geiger-counter**__.

__
 
• **Geiger-counter** is the m**ost common instrument** for measuring radiation.
 
• For detecting and measuring radiation, many laboratory instruments are used.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Human senses** cannot **detect radiation**.
 
• In **Geiger-counter**, **electric pulses **are created when a high voltage is applied.
 
• These pulses give the reading on the instrument.
 
• **Micrometre** with **sodium iodide detector **is also used for** measuring radiation**.
 
• In this, the electric signal is produced by pulse and light.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A portable multichannel analyser is also used to detect radioactive materials.
 
• The ionisation chamber is also used to detect radiation.
 
• Neutron REM metre is also used to detect radiation.

questions.question: Which of the following is the hottest planet of our solar system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​__**Venus**__.

__
 
• Venus is the** hottest planet** in **our solar system**.
 
• This **planet inhibits** a very dense **atmosphere.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Generally, the planets** which are nearest **to the **sun are hotter**.
 
• But the **planet Venus** is an exception to this.
 
• Venus has a **surface temperature** of about **888 degrees F**.
 
• Earth has a **surface temperature **of **61 degrees F**.
 
• **When the distance increases **from the sun, the **surface temperature** of th**e planet decreases**.
 
• The** dense atmosphere** contributes to the heating of Venus by acting like a **greenhouse.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **Hint__**

questions.question: The metals that produce a sound on striking a hard surface are called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**sonorous**__.

__
 
• The **metals that produce** a sound on **striking a hard surface **are calle**d sonorous metals**.
 
• When we strike these metals, a ringing sound is produced.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• These metals have **extremely low negativity**.
 
• The electrons in these metals are not bounded so much and they are delocalised.
 
• The** ****electrons cloud moves** in an easy way.
 
• The **energy is dissipated** less.
 
• The **kinetic energy** is produced and the sound we hear, when striking on these metals.
 
• The most sonorous metal is silver.
 
• The elasticity of silver is high.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Copper, iron, calcium and magnesium are also sonorous.
 
• Sonorous metals are also good conductors of heat.

questions.question: In the context of Mughal administration, the term ‘polaj’ stood for a:

• For each crop, the polaj was cultivated in succession.

• To measure** land, illahi gaj** was made a **definite uni**t.

• In the entire empire, the most ideal type of land was polaj.
